page: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32gb is an x86_64 cloud server within the VX1 Cloud Compute family, configured with dedicated AMD EPYC processor resources and a memory-heavy allocation profile. The hardware configuration features 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2.0 GHz, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 vector support (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16) along with hardware cryptography features such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio that classifies it within memory-optimized operating parameters. Local storage is limited to a minimal 1 GB NVMe SSD volume, intended primarily for core OS environments or minimal state, requiring remote or volume-attached block storage for persistent data. One complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled, with no discrete GPU accelerators present.

Benchmark testing demonstrates high single-threaded efficiency alongside moderate overall multi-core scalability. In single-core execution, the server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng (3,621.37) as well as gzip compression throughput (39.66 GB/sec) and bzip3 single-threaded decompression (17.59 GB/sec). Conversely, Geekbench multi-core performance (4,109.0) and Clang software compilation (5,150.0) place in the bottom 25%, reflecting the physical two-core hardware ceiling under saturated parallel computational loads.

Throughput for memory-bound and caching operations is consistent, with Redis SET benchmarks registering 8.06 million operations per second and static web serving delivering 14.6 GB/sec. Lightweight inference with a 135M parameter LLM reaches 197.53 text generation tokens per second, but throughput drops significantly to 15.98 tokens per second on 7B prompt processing. The vx1-m-4c-32gb is well suited for memory-intensive caching layers, in-memory databases, text manipulation, and microservices requiring dedicated per-vCPU stability without heavy sustained multi-core compute.
description: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32gb is a memory-optimized cloud instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, it supplies 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, accompanied by 32 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction support. The server includes 32.0 GB of system memory, producing an expansive 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD and one public IPv4 address. Single-core processing demonstrates top-tier throughput in compression and stress-ng evaluations, while parallel throughput is bounded by the physical core count, resulting in average-to-low multi-threaded Geekbench scores. Achieving 8.06 million Redis SET operations per second and 14.6 GB/sec in static web serving, the platform offers balanced efficiency for in-memory caching, key-value data stores, text processing, and intermediate memory-bound application tiers.
